task: NBA Physical Attributes Impact on Career Performance

data_sources.draft_fallback: NBA Database/draft_history.csv (loaded only as plan-documented fallback; NOT required - 0 of the matched players needed a draft-round backfill)

pipeline: 2. Clean combine: drop 3 rows with player_id<=0, sort by season, drop_duplicates(player_id, keep='last') -> 1175 unique players.
3. INNER join combine.player_id == common_player_info.person_id -> 691 rows / 691 unique players.
4. career_span_years = to_year - from_year + 1; 0 rows dropped for undefined span.
5. Valid-career filter 0 <= career_span_years <= 25 -> 0 rows dropped (observed range 1-21).
6. draft_round_num = to_numeric(draft_round, errors='coerce'), values outside [1,10] -> NaN ('Undrafted', missing, sentinel 0) -> 571 valid players (Round 1: 337, Round 2: 234).
7. Height backfill: parse master 'H-ft' string ('6-10' -> 82 in) and fill 20 missing height_wo_shoes values.
9. Pearson r + two-sided p (scipy.stats.pearsonr) for each attribute vs draft_round_num and vs career_span_years, pairwise-complete (per-attribute n, no global listwise drop).
10. composite_score = -correlation_with_draft + correlation_with_career (no manual sign flip for sprint; raw coefficient used).
12. Wrote output.csv (4 rows, 7 columns) and physical_attributes_analysis.png (2x2, figsize 14x11, dpi 150) from the SAME in-memory numbers so CSV and figure annotations cannot drift.
method.environment_note: matplotlib was not present in the system python; a throw-away virtualenv at /tmp/venv (pandas, numpy, scipy, matplotlib 3.11.2) was used to render the figure. All numbers come from the same script (analyze.py).

findings.draft_round: Height (r=-0.101, p=0.015) and 3/4 court sprint (r=+0.124, p=0.007) are the only attributes significantly related to draft round; both act in the athletic direction (taller -> better/lower round, faster -> better/lower round). Wingspan is marginal (r=-0.070, p=0.099) and max vertical leap is not significant (r=-0.018, p=0.700).
findings.career_span: No physical attribute shows a statistically significant relationship with career span (all |r| <= 0.048, all p >= 0.21). Career longevity in this sample is essentially uncorrelated with combine measurables.
findings.weights: Normalized weights: 3/4 Court Sprint 37.7%, Height 36.1%, Wingspan 24.5%, Max Vertical Leap 1.7%. Sprint and Height dominate because their draft coefficients are the largest in magnitude; Max Vertical Leap gets a near-zero weight because its draft and career coefficients almost cancel (composite -0.0069). Note the composite for sprint is NEGATIVE (-0.156) since its correlation with draft round is positive (slower = later round); per the plan this raw sign is preserved in the formula, so the weight reflects magnitude, not direction.

notes: Matched unique players = 691, exactly as planned (rows = 691 because combine was de-duplicated before the join).
Combine unique players = 1175 vs the plan's 1176 (1 fewer); no effect on any downstream number.

Height pairwise n (571 for draft, 691 for career) is slightly HIGHER than the plan's expectations (553/671) because the 20 backfilled heights are included, per plan step 7 ordering. All other pairwise n match the plan exactly (wingspan 554/672, vertical 479/585, sprint 477/583).
All 4 normalized weights >= 0 and sum to 1.0.

limitations: Draft round is effectively binary (Round 1 vs Round 2) in the 2001+ combine era, so correlation_with_draft is a point-biserial on a restricted range - a coarse draft-capital proxy. Sensitivity check vs continuous draft_number gives the same ordering of effects (height r=-0.130 p=0.002, sprint r=+0.107 p=0.020, wingspan r=-0.107 p=0.012, vertical r=-0.034 p=0.456).
Survivorship/selection bias: athleticism is measured only for combine invitees, 691 of 1175 invitees (58.8%) matched an NBA record.
Career span is right-censored for players still active at the data snapshot, which attenuates the career correlations.
Univariate Pearson correlations do not control for position, entry age or era; sprint is inverted (lower = faster) so its composite sign must be read with care.
Per-attribute pairwise n differs (477-691), so each weight comes from a slightly different sample.
